summary: Census of all publicly available ternary/BitNet-family causal LMs as of 2026-07-17, using the HF Hub as authoritative registry. The zero-training frontier splits into three tiers. (1) Fleet-wide tier: tiiuae Falcon-E-3B-Instruct (Apr 2025, never in program docs) is confirmed as the sleeper — pure LlamaForCausalLM (RMSNorm/RoPE/GQA 16q-2kv/SwiGLU, vocab 32768, untied head, BitNet per-tensor packing identical to the Falcon-E-1B already running in the engine), ~3.05B params, three revisions (main packed / bfloat16 / prequantized, so a trainable bf16 master exists), and TII's published table shows it beating the canonical microsoft/bitnet-b1.58-2B-4T (avg 22.65 vs 17.70 on the same 6-task Leaderboard-v2 suite) at a computed ALICE runtime of ~1.55GB (730MB packed + 268MB f32 embed + 268MB f32 head + 268MB KV@4096) — it fits even the 2GB pre-AVX2 machines at reduced context, which BitNet-2B cannot do without vocab pruning (its f32 embeddings alone are 1.31GB). (2) Dev-box tier: HF1BitLLM/Llama3-8B-1.58-100B-tokens (already on the external drive) remains the largest drop-in-compatible checkpoint (~4.9GB with f16 embeddings; f32 embeddings would blow the 6.5GB VM). (3) Stretch tier: the NEW prism-ml Ternary-Bonsai family (Apr-Jul 2026, Apache-2.0, Qwen3-based, natively ternary-trained) is by far the highest-capability public ternary line — Bonsai-8B self-reports avg 75.5 vs Qwen3-8B's 79.3 with a 2.18GB Q2_0 GGUF — but is NOT drop-in: it uses one FP16 scale per group of 128 weights (engine is per-tensor) and Qwen3 QK-norm (engine lacks it), so porting requires two bounded kernel additions, not a rewrite; the Bonsai-27B (Qwen3.6 hybrid attention) is out of scope. Everything else — 1bitLLM repro 700M/1.3B/3B (MIT), SpectraSuite TriLMs 99M-3.9B (Apache-2.0, base-only, 300B tokens), Falcon3-1B/3B/7B/10B-1.58bit (PTQ-derived, settled-finding degraded) — is quality-dominated. Also noted: microsoft released bitnet-embedding-0.6b/270m on 2026-07-15 (embedding models, not causal LMs); no BitNet-v2 generative weights exist publicly. Falcon-E '1B' is actually 1.8B params per TII's own table.

summary: The onebitllms path is real, small, and directly compatible with the existing engine pipeline. The toolkit (github.com/tiiuae/onebitllms, v0.0.4, Apr 2026, 16 commits) is a thin layer: (1) replace_linear_with_bitnet_linear() swaps every nn.Linear EXCEPT lm_head for a BitNetLinear doing straight-through-estimator fake-quant (per-tensor absmean ternary weights, per-token int8 activations) via Triton kernels; (2) it plugs into stock TRL SFTTrainer; (3) quantize_to_1bit() exports using transformers' own integrations.pack_weights + weight_scale with scale = 1/mean(|w|) — byte-for-byte the same packed BitNet format and reciprocal-scale convention as the Falcon-E `main` revision that aegis-forge/repack_ternary.py already consumes. Both Falcon-E-1B-Base and Falcon-E-1B-Instruct ship `prequantized` (bf16 unpacked, train from this), `bfloat16`, and `main` (packed) revisions; config is pure LlamaForCausalLM (24L, d=2048, 16H/2KV GQA, SwiGLU 9216, RoPE theta 1e6, vocab 32768, untied embeddings) — exactly the engine's supported family. LoRA/PEFT is explicitly NOT supported (full-FT only, stated by TII and Axolotl). The recipe is CUDA-only (Triton + torch.cuda.device hardcoded), so the Chromebook cannot run it natively and Kaggle P100 (sm_6.0 < Triton's sm_7.0 floor) and Kaggle TPU (no Triton on XLA) are out; Colab/Kaggle T4 is the viable free target, with one open risk: TII's example uses bf16 and T4 has no native bf16 (fp32-fallback or fp16 must be smoke-tested). Arithmetic says a 5M-token SFT epoch on one T4 is ~2-6 hours — trivially inside Kaggle's ~30h/week — versus ~1-2 weeks off-recipe on the Chromebook CPU with a swapfile and a hand-written CPU BitLinear. TII publishes no catastrophic-forgetting guidance; standard replay mixing must be self-imposed.

chromebook_verdict: Chromebook-native: NO for the official toolkit (CUDA/Triton hardcoded). Off-recipe CPU port is arithmetic-possible but marginal: N≈1.72B params; training cost 6N≈10.3 GFLOP/token; i5-10210U sustained PyTorch fp32 training realistically 20-50 GFLOPS (peak AVX2 FMA ~270 GFLOPS, 4C@~2.1GHz all-core x 32 FLOP/cyc) → 2-5 tok/s → ~170-430K tok/day compute-bound. RAM: fp32 weights 6.9GB + grads 6.9GB + Adafactor states ~0.1GB ≈ 14GB working set vs 6.5GB visible RAM → needs a ~16-24GB swapfile (disk has 38GB free); per-optimizer-step swap traffic ~14GB ≈ 2-3 min at ~100MB/s, amortized over 16K-token accumulation steps (~1-2h compute each) so I/O is not the bottleneck. Net: a 1M-token SFT ≈ 3-8 days, 5M ≈ 2-5 weeks — inside the unlimited-wall-clock envelope but requires writing/validating a custom CPU BitLinear (STE math verified from source, ~6 lines) and surviving swap fragility. Free cloud from the browser: YES, and vastly better — single Kaggle/Colab T4 (15-16GB): 5M tokens x 10.3 GFLOP = 5.2e16 FLOPs; at 3-8 effective TFLOPS (fp32/fp16 with ~20% QAT overhead) → 2-5 hours, one session, well under Kaggle's ~30h/week. VRAM: weights 3.45GB (bf16-stored) + grads 3.45GB + 8-bit Adam 3.45GB + grad-ckpt activations ~1GB ≈ 11-12GB → fits 15GB T4 (Adafactor drops it to ~8.5GB). Kaggle T4x2 gives headroom via DDP/ZeRO; P100 and TPU are eliminated (Triton). Artifact flow is Chromebook-friendly: quantize_to_1bit output ~0.6-0.9GB packed → download or push to HF → repack_ternary.py locally (fits 6.5GB RAM/38GB disk).

summary: BitNet-2B-4T specialization is viable at zero budget — but only via free cloud GPU, not the Chromebook CPU. microsoft/bitnet-b1.58-2B-4T-bf16 (2.41B params, master weights) exists on HF, is explicitly designated "Use this only for training or fine-tuning purposes," and — decisively — its config.json sets quantization_config {quant_method: bitnet, linear_class: autobitlinear, quantization_mode: "online"}, which makes transformers' native BitNet integration run fake-quant QAT (ternary absmean weight quant + int8 activation quant) with a Straight-Through Estimator (WeightQuant autograd.Function, verified by reading the source) on every forward pass. Standard trl SFTTrainer/DPOTrainer therefore fine-tune it directly; no onebitllms needed (onebitllms/Axolotl officially support only Falcon-E anyway), and SubLN is baked into the BitNetForCausalLM architecture class so it complicates nothing. Community proof exists: jpacifico's Aramis-2B-BitNet (bilingual DPO + TIES/ModelStock merges from the bf16 master) reports ARC-C +3.67, ARC-E +1.81, Winogrande +1.42, TriviaQA +3.11 over base and shipped as ternary i2s GGUF; several LoRA adapters (e.g. UlukaDev roman-numeral: 0%→24.2% exact match) also exist. Microsoft provides NO official FT code (bitnet.cpp is inference-only; GitHub FT issues go unanswered) — the working recipe is pure transformers+trl at ~10x normal learning rate. Hardware floor: full FT needs ~14.5GB minimum (bf16 weights 4.83 + bf16 grads 4.83 + 8-bit Adam 4.83) plus activations — marginal on one free Colab T4 (16GB), comfortable on Kaggle's free 2xT4 (32GB, 30h/week, 12h sessions) with grad checkpointing; a 10-20M-token SFT is roughly 3-10 GPU-hours there. Chromebook CPU full FT fails on disk arithmetic alone (needs ~16GB swap + 4.8GB model + ~10GB checkpoints vs 38GB free, at ~1-2 tok/s swap-thrashed). The Falcon-E blog's warning that naive bf16-FT-then-requantize degrades quality is mooted here because the online-mode STE means you are never training in plain bf16 — the forward pass is always ternary.

pitfalls: T4 GPUs (Colab and Kaggle free) do not support bf16 — you must train in fp16 AMP with an fp32 master copy or full fp32; QAT at 10x learning rate in fp16 can overflow, so monitor GradScaler and consider fp32 for the WeightQuant path (transformers already computes it in float32 internally).
Learning rate is the documented failure mode: community issue #295 used lr 5e-7 and loss never moved; TII's guidance for BitNet fine-tuning is ~10x a normal LLM LR. Start around 1e-4.

Gains measured on the bf16-side model can shrink after the ternary snap: always re-evaluate PPL/task metrics on the re-quantized, repacked engine artifact. Aramis's 'lossless from BF16' GGUF claim is plausible (master weights sit near ternary attractors after QAT) but unverified.

LoRA adapters on the bf16 master work at train time but may be partially erased when merged and re-quantized (per-tensor absmean rounding swallows sub-half-step deltas), and raw adapters cannot run in the ternary engine at all. Prefer full-parameter QAT; treat LoRA-merge-requantize as an experiment needing before/after eval.
Do not fine-tune from microsoft/bitnet-b1.58-2B-4T (packed): its config is quantization_mode 'offline' with non-trainable uint8 weight buffers.

The bf16 repo's auto_map references modeling_bitnet.py files that are not in the repo — load WITHOUT trust_remote_code on a recent transformers (>=4.52-era native 'bitnet' model type); pin the transformers version in the Kaggle notebook.

2B-4T is already SFT+DPO aligned (and Microsoft never released the pre-SFT base — issue #352 unanswered); aggressive domain SFT will cause chat-ability forgetting. Mix general instruct data and keep token budgets modest.

transformers' native BitNet integration implements WeightQuant(torch.autograd.Function): forward = absmean per-tensor ternary round-clamp, backward = grad_output.clone() (STE); online-mode BitLinear also carries an optional RMSNorm on pre-quant activations (the SubLN), so SubLN requires no special handling in trainers.

Microsoft provides no official fine-tuning code: bitnet.cpp is inference-only, and GitHub issues asking about fine-tuning (Korean SFT stuck at loss 3.3-3.6 with lr 5e-7, #295; 'is bf16 pre-SFT?' #352) sit unanswered by maintainers.

summary: Training a tiny ternary model from scratch is the one path that is fully verified feasible on this Chromebook alone, and I measured it directly on the box rather than estimating: a llama-style BitNet-QAT training step (RMSNorm+RoPE+SwiGLU BitLinear, absmean STE fake-quant, AdamW, tied head, torch 2.13 CPU, 8 threads) runs at 733 tok/s for an 8.5M-param model, 458 tok/s at 21M, and 138 tok/s at 47M — i.e., 63M/40M/12M tokens per day, ~40-60 effective GFLOPS against a measured 75-117 GFLOPS raw matmul ceiling. External evidence says tiny ternary QAT works: Spectra/TriLM trained ternary llama-style models from 99M up on 300B tokens with checkpoints public; BitNet b1.58 Reloaded studied 100K-48M ternary models and found they reach fp-level quality when hidden sizes are roughly doubled (the "ternary tax" at small scale — parity without tricks only emerges near 3B); and a Feb 2026 paper (TernaryLM) already trained a 132M native-ternary model on TinyStories to 58.4 val PPL, so the ternary-TinyStories idea is no longer virgin territory — but no sub-50M ternary TinyStories model was found, so a 5-15M ternary storyteller that boots bare-metal with no OS remains an unclaimed, publishable first. Free accelerators multiply the frontier ~1000x: Kaggle now offers TPU v5e-8 (replaced v3-8 in 2025, ~20 hr/week, 9-hr sessions, background execution), making a Chinchilla-trained 125M ternary model (~1.9e18 FLOPs) a one-to-two-week-of-quota job; Colab free T4 covers the same in ~2 weeks of babysat sessions; TRC remains open to solo researchers on a rolling basis with a publish-your-results expectation. No CPU trainer showed verified >2x-torch throughput at this size class — torch/oneDNN is already at ~25-50% of this thermally-limited chip's practical peak, so the lever is free TPU, not a different framework. Practical frontier: ~15M params to Chinchilla in 1 week local, ~30-40M in 1 month local, ~125M on Kaggle free quota.
load_bearing_claim: Ternary (1.58-bit) quantization-aware training reaches or surpasses full-precision quality even at 100K-48M parameters when hidden layer sizes are roughly doubled relative to the fp16 twin (BitNet b1.58 Reloaded, https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.09527) — this is what makes a useful sub-50M ternary model possible at all, and it quantifies the ~2x-width tax the training plan must budget for, since Spectra (https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.12327) shows free parity only near 3B.

TinyStories-style convergence (~0.3-0.5B domain tokens) for a 10-15M model: ~5-12 days. Practical frontier: (a) 1 week ≈ 15M params, (b) 1 month ≈ 30-40M params. TRACK A (local, start now, pure sovereignty): train a ~10-15M ternary TinyStories model entirely on the Chromebook — custom 4k-8k BPE vocab trained on the corpus, llama-family config compatible with aegis-forge (d=256-320, L=8-10, heads=8, SwiGLU BitLinear with absmean/reciprocal-scale convention matching repack_ternary.py, SubLN per BitNet-2B-4T, fp embeddings/norms/tied head, ctx 512-1024), two-stage LR + weight-decay-to-zero per the Era-of-1-bit training-tips recipe, ~300-500M TinyStories tokens, 5-12 days wall-clock. pitfalls: The small-scale ternary tax is real: Spectra shows parity only near 3B; at 10-100M budget ~2x hidden width (BitNet Reloaded) vs the fp16 twin, so quality targets must be set against a half-size float model, not a same-size one

summary: Data distillation (downloading teacher-generated corpora) is the strongest and cheapest capability-injection lever for this program, and the key assets are free, permissively licensed, and small enough for the Chromebook's 38GB disk. The decisive precedent is SmolLM2: its post-training used SmolTalk (~1.1M samples, Apache-2.0), which in the paper's own 1.7B-scale ablations beat OpenHermes-2.5 and Magpie-Pro on IFEval/MT-Bench, and HF shipped a capacity-filtered variant for sub-1B models — exactly the recipe the falcon-sft (onebitllms QAT SFT) path needs. Logit-level KD is real but modest (+1 to +3 points over SFT in published 1B-student ablations e.g. DistillLens on TinyLlama-1.1B, and Llama-3.2-1B used it), but it is blocked here twice over: Falcon-E's 32,678-token custom vocab is incompatible with any Llama-3-vocab teacher for direct KD, and a free-tier T4 cannot co-host an 8B teacher plus a 1B full-fine-tune student. The creative option (running HF1BitLLM Llama3-8B-1.58 as a local teacher at ~2.5 tok/s) is arithmetically dead as a bulk source: ~1.5M tokens/week means ~463 days to generate a modest 100M-token corpus, and the teacher itself is a degraded PTQ-recovery model (behind fp16 Llama3-8B; TII positions Falcon-E-3B as competitive with it) — strictly worse than downloading Mixtral/GPT-4o-generated corpora that already exist. Claude-as-teacher is blocked by Anthropic's current Consumer Terms (effective 2025-10-08), which prohibit using the Services "to develop or train any artificial intelligence or machine learning algorithms or models"; for a DARPA-facing project where data provenance will be scrutinized, Claude outputs must not enter training data (Claude remains fine for tooling, filtering scripts, and eval harnesses). LIMA/LIMIT evidence says 1k-10k curated examples buy style/format alignment, not capability, at 1B scale anyway — so the ToS-blocked path was low-value regardless. This week's action: download SmolTalk + Tulu-3 SFT mixture (minus its CC-BY-NC No Robots subset) + a small Cosmopedia-v2 slice, under 10GB total, and build the filtered ~300-500M-token SFT mix locally for the free-GPU QAT-SFT runs.
